selectedItems.title: [STVL] New Obstruction Zones!
selectedItems.summary: Howdy everyone - your friendly neighborhood navigator here! I wanted to let you know quickly about a new feature in STVL that I think is very useful for the community - Obstruction Zones ! Courtesy of Remco , these allow you to specify occlusions to your sensors to treat them specially in the decay functions so that they remain present when in-bounds of the sensor frustum so they aren’t actively decayed. STVL was originally designed with high-visibility sensor configurations in mind (8+ RGBD cameras; top mounted 3D lidar) so this is a wonderful addition for those with dead areas in the sensor FOV due to self-collision or similar. Pull request SteveMacenski/spatio_temporal_voxel_layer [ros2] added obstruction polygons to 3d lidar frustrum (#367) ros2 ← remco-r:feature/ros2_obstruction_polygons remco-r opened 08:22PM - 21 Oct 26 UTC +687 -12 ## Add FOV Obstruction Polygons for 3D Lidar Frustum I introduced the option … to add "obstruction polygons" to the 3D lidar frustum. This way obstructions which are part of the robot body are considered out of field of view and persist accordingly.

selectedItems.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model
selectedItems.articleText: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model Oct 28, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Gemini 4 Carbon is our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. Koray Kavukcuoglu SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Today, we’re announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching. On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates. Building on Gemini 4 Argon , which was launched two weeks ago, Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward. Our researchers and models are working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster, while strengthening our safeguards in tandem. We're taking a deliberate approach to rollout and are actively engaged in the U.S. government’s voluntary process for pre-release model testing. Starting this week, we will make Carbon available to a subset of cyber defenders and will gradually phase access to additional trusted partners through our Fairwind Program . We’re continuing to gather feedback and iterate on guardrails before making Carbon available to developers, businesses, and consumers via our product surfaces as soon as possible. Gemini 4 Carbon will launch at the same introductory price 1 as Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price. Improving coding and reasoning for challenging, long-horizon tasks Designed to take on much harder, long-horizon engineering problems, Carbon is built for sustained agentic workflows. Internally, our teams have seen Carbon run for days to persist through dead ends to tackle complex, multi-step engineering tasks like root-causing and patching subtle bugs across large codebases and low-level systems. Building on user feedback, we focused on improving model performance across a variety of domains, including coding, agentic, and scientific tasks, as well as full-stack web development and multimodal understanding. With improved quality of output and artifacts in web development, Carbon jumps +89 elo points to land at #4 (1768) on WebDev Arena . State-of-the-art cybersecurity performance to help build secure systems Gemini 4 Carbon delivers a significant leap in cybersecurity capabilities. It achieves state-of-the-art performance across the cybersecurity defense lifecycle — vulnerability detection, validation, and remediation. Our teams are already seeing strong gains in cyberdefense. On internal benchmarks, Carbon achieves more than 2x uplift in success rate for generating secure code over Argon. As another example, the Chrome team has reported that Carbon performed more than 10X better than another lab's large frontier model when generating high quality patches. Wiz, our leading Cloud security platform, also observes Carbon leading on benchmarks for web penetration testing, a core capability for Wiz's Scan for Good initiative. Carbon excels across key external benchmarks (evaluated without guardrails): Finding real vulnerabilities: Core to cybersecurity defense is finding real vulnerabilities. Carbon achieves a state-of-the-art 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro , autonomously uncovering complex flaws buried in real-world software. Validating risk through exploitation: To prioritize which vulnerabilities to remediate first or remediate at all, cyber defenders increasingly rely on models to check which vulnerabilities are exploitable. Carbon sets a new state-of-the-art on the popular exploitation benchmark ExploitGym (54.8%). Patching at the root cause: Ultimately after identifying the vulnerabilities, fixing the root cause is a critical step in the cybersecurity defense lifecycle. Carbon reaches 71.0% on Collinear’s CWE-bench , turning validated findings directly into working code fixes. Advancing frontier model safety & security Gemini 4 Carbon builds on the same multi-layered safety and security stack of Argon — combining model training, real-time misuse defenses, prompt-injection resilience, and chain-of-thought monitoring. In particular, we made significant strides in model alignment with Argon, and reported its propensities to behave in an aligned way in our Safety and Security report . With Carbon, we challenged ourselves to go a step further on alignment, and trained the model to respond to complex or high-pressure tasks in the right way. Reducing shortcuts and loophole exploitation: With Carbon, we further mitigated shortcut attempts in training while ensuring high-quality coding performance. Carbon reduced successful cheating on Terminal-Bench 4.0 to 0.0%, with attempts to cheat dropping to 0.4% — all while improving overall accuracy. In live coding environments with our internal teams, we observed that high-severity misalignment alerts dropped by almost 80%. Greater transparency and honesty: In our internal testing, Carbon cuts unsupported claims by approximately 2x over Argon. It puts methodological caveats directly into the deliverable or withholds blocked actions with a clear list of what remains required, rather than fabricating or hedging around missing evidence. Improved collaboration with the user in the face of ambiguity: Rather than guessing or forcing a path forward, Carbon retrieves the relevant sources and surfaces discrepancies to the user before acting — as a result, users should observe a much better collaborative experience with Carbon. Following through without overstepping: Carbon simultaneously reduced overreach by 26% and under-service by 29% resulting in much more reliable execution of multi-step plans end-to-end while respecting project constraints and staying strictly within scope. Resisting prompt injection: While Argon previously led the Gray Swan’s Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) Benchmark in prompt injection resistance with a very low 0.7% attack success rate, Carbon achieves 0.0% — resisting every evaluated attack attempt. Coming soon to developers, businesses, and consumers Pushing the frontier forward requires moving fast while remaining deliberate about deployment. With Gemini 4 Carbon, our goal is to deliver meaningful leaps in software engineering and cybersecurity defense without compromising on safety or reliability. We’re eager to see how the initial cohort of cyber defenders use this model and we look forward to bringing Carbon to developers, businesses, and consumers soon. ## Security: Node.js runtime and CA certificate updates (October 2026)

On October 20, 2026, eMudhra disclosed that the private keys for eight of its intermediate CA certificates could be recovered from the public certificates. On October 21, Node.js shipped [security releases](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases) that update its bundled CA certificates for the compromise and fix several unrelated high-severity runtime CVEs. On October 23, Python's `certifi` 2026.10.23 removed the eMudhra roots `emSign Root CA - C1` and `emSign ECC Root CA - C3`.

**How these servers stand**

- **The TypeScript servers rely on the Node.js runtime for certificate checks.** They ship no CA certificates of their own. Only `server-everything` makes outbound HTTPS requests (`gzip-file-as-resource`), and the Node.js it runs on verifies them. `server-filesystem`, `server-memory` and `server-sequential-thinking` make no network connections.
- **`mcp-server-fetch` verifies HTTPS against the `certifi` bundle**, through `httpx`. Installing from PyPI (`uvx mcp-server-fetch`, `pip install mcp-server-fetch`) resolves the current `certifi`, 2026.10.23 or later. The repository's `fetch` Dockerfile installs from its lockfile, which this release moves to `certifi` 2026.10.23 (#5341).
- **`mcp-server-git` and `mcp-server-time` make no network connections.**

**If you run a TypeScript server from npm (`npx` or a global install)**

It runs on your Node.js, which we can't update for you. Please run Node.js **24.22.1 or 26.12.1, or later**, and check with `node --version`. The packages' `engines` field accepts any Node.js 24, so npm won't warn you about an older, unpatched runtime.

**If you run `mcp-server-fetch` from an existing environment**

An environment created before October 23 keeps its older `certifi`. Refresh it with `uvx --refresh mcp-server-fetch`, or `pip install -U certifi`.

selectedItems.articleText: While automotive OEM orders declined in the first half of 2026, they picked up in Q3. Source: A3 North American companies ordered 10,989 robots valued at $723.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, according to the latest data from the Association for Advancing Automation, or A3. Orders increased 24.8% in units and 26.1% in value compared with the third quarter of 2025, making it the strongest quarter of the year so far, it said. The third-quarter gains pushed total orders for the first nine months of 2026 to 28,984 robots valued at approximately $1.89 billion, A3 reported. This represented increases of 9.6% in units and 13.3% in value over the same period last year , noted the Ann Arbor, Mich.-based organization . Orders grow in automotive in addition to other industries After declining during the first half of 2026, automotive OEM robot orders returned to positive year-over-year growth in the third quarter, increasing 7.5%, said A3. Orders from automotive component suppliers climbed 90.4%, continuing the strong demand from that segment seen earlier in the year. Several other industries recorded substantial increases in robot orders during Q3: Semiconductors and electronics /photonics: +97.6% units Plastics and rubber: +67.7% units Life sciences /pharmaceutical /biomedical : +38.7% units Metals: +37.0% units All other industries increased just 0.5% in units ordered, while food and consumer goods declined by 23.7%, A3 added. The growth in the electronics segment occurred as investment grew in U.S. semiconductor manufacturing, with strong demand for electronics supporting AI and other applications. Life sciences has also seen continued investment in domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing among others, said A3. Automotive component orders were particularly strong despite earlier weakness among automotive manufacturing, said the organization. While OEM orders improved in Q3, they remained 17% below their year-earlier level through the first nine months of 2026. “What stands out in the third quarter is not simply the magnitude of the growth, but how broadly it was distributed across the market,” stated Alex Shikany, executive vice president at A3. “Automotive OEM orders returned to positive growth, while automotive components and sectors such as semiconductors/electronics and life sciences posted significant gains. That broader mix is important because it points to a robotics market that is becoming increasingly diversified across industries and applications.” Submit your innovation now! Cobot orders increase 56%, finds A3 Force- and power-limited or collaborative robots also posted a strong third quarter, with 1,831 units valued at $63.8 million ordered. This was an increase of about 56% in units compared with Q3 2025. Collaborative robots accounted for 16.7% of all robot units ordered during the quarter. Through September, North American companies ordered 4,605 cobots valued at approximately $178 million, representing 15.9% of total robot units and 9.4% of order value. Collaborative robots continue to be used across a wide range of applications and industries. In the first nine months of 2026, cobots accounted for 43.8% of robot orders in life sciences/pharma/biomed and 36.9% in semi & electronics/photonics. Manufacturing activity continues expansion The stronger robot order numbers come alongside improving manufacturing activity, said A3. The September Institute of Supply Chain Management (ISM) Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) registered 54.5, marking a ninth consecutive month of expansion, while the Federal Reserve said that U.S. manufacturing output increasing 0.3% in September. Higher input costs, trade uncertainty, and the timing of large manufacturing projects remain factors to watch, noted A3. “But with robot orders strengthening across several industries, the North American market enters the final quarter of 2026 with positive momentum,” it said. More detailed Q3 2026 market data and graphs are available upon request for press and through the A3 Vault for member companies. selectedItems.articleText: Warp Sciences plans to create chemistry infrastructure for sovereign biotech. Source: deni AI, Adobe Stock Warp Sciences last week emerged from stealth with $215 million in funding to create infrastructure that enables biotech and pharmaceutical companies to discover new medicines faster. The startup said it is building a U.S.-based chemistry contract research organization, or CRO, to bring together chemists, robotics, and AI to make and test molecules for research teams. The South San Francisco-based company ‘s stated goal is to provide experimental data to train better AI that in turn enables more capable labs, giving scientists the ability to test more ideas. “AI has dramatically accelerated software engineering and mathematics, but it has yet to make the same impact in the physical sciences,” stated Kevin Weil , co-founder and CEO of Warp Sciences. “Chemistry and biology move forward when you make something, test it and learn from the result.” “If we want to build more capable AI for science, we need to generate real-world data at scale,” he added. “Warp is starting that process by making the research compounds drug discovery needs today, while building the labs and automation to speed the cycle from hypothesis to experiment to answer.” Warp said it has no proprietary drug pipeline itself; it is designing automated labs that can run experiments, learn from them, and improve with each cycle. Warp Sciences focuses on sovereign biotechnology A promising molecular design is only the beginning, observed Warp Sciences. “Scientists have to make it, test it, and use what they learn to decide what comes next,” said the company. “Faster access to compounds gives research teams faster answers, more ideas to pursue, and more opportunities to find medicines that change lives.” Warp also noted the importance of sovereign biotechnology. In a 2024 survey by the Biotechnology Innovation Organization, 74% reported contracts with Chinese companies for preclinical and clinical services, according to Reuters. The BIOSECURE Act , signed into law in December 2025, established a framework for restrictions on federal procurement and funding involving designated biotechnology companies of concern. In response, Warp claimed that it is building a U.S.-based chemistry partner that scientists can rely on for its speed, quality, and close collaboration. Its goal is to shorten the path from molecular design to testing while giving customers more control over where sensitive research takes place. The company said its initial service will focus on lead optimization analog synthesis, making variations of molecules that scientists can compare as they search for a drug candidate. Experienced chemists will guide experiments as the lab is increasingly automated by robotics and AI, with AI models trained on data from physical experiments. Warp plans to enable its customers to discover drugs more efficiently and keep that discovery in the U.S. Submit your innovation now! Founders’ expertise spans AI and healthcare Warp Sciences noted that its founding team ’s experience spans AI, data infrastructure, healthcare, and drug discovery. Weil most recently served as chief product officer and vice president of science at OpenAI . Chief Scientific Officer Solomon “Sol” Reisberg held medicinal chemistry leadership roles at Terremoto Biosciences. “I’ve worked with overseas chemistry partners that delivered speed and value, but I still worried about protecting the intellectual property behind our programs,” said Reisberg. “We’re building Warp to give drug hunters that same caliber of chemistry services in the U.S., with IP protection at the center of the relationship, and without the price premium that U.S. boutique CROs currently demand.” Chief Technology Officer “Manohar “Mano” Paluri was a vice president at Meta Superintelligence Labs and a founding member of FAIR. DJ Patil was a founding executive at Devoted Health and the first U.S. chief data scientist for the White House. “Our goal is simple: Every experiment should make the next one smarter,” Paluri asserted. “AI needs a closer connection to the physical work of chemistry. Closing the loop between designing experiments, executing them, and learning from their outcomes builds increasingly capable systems for deciding what to make and how to make it. We’re building the software, AI and robotics alongside the lab so each part is shaped by what chemists actually need.” Early hires have added robotics experience from companies including Genesis , Skild AI , and 1X Technologies , as well as scientific expertise from Genentech and Lawrence Livermore National Labs. “Warp’s services bolster customer-led discovery programs. Our biotech and pharma customers determine which molecules to pursue and retain control of their drug programs,” said Patil. “We’re not developing drugs of our own. We’re building the infrastructure for the people who do.” Venture capital firms, angel investors support Warp Lightspeed led Warp Sciences’ funding, with participation from Premji Invest, Mayfield, IVP, Lux, Conviction, Menlo Ventures, 01 Advisors, Standard, Lowercarbon Capital, Gigascale Capital, Angular Ventures, Scribble Ventures, Uncork Capital, Innovation Endeavors, Matter VP, Zero Shot Fund, SignalFire and Moxxie Ventures. Angel investors included Brian Armstrong (Coinbase CEO), Mike Krieger (Anthropic Labs co-lead, Instagram co-founder), Milan Kovac (former Tesla Robotics vice president), and Ion Stoica (Databricks co-founder). It also included Fidji Simo (former OpenAI AGI Deployment CEO), Brendan Foody (Mercor CEO), Mark Chen (OpenAI chief research officer), and Sarah Friar (OpenAI chief financial officer). In addition, Kate Rouch (former OpenAI and Coinbase chief marketing officer), Lulu Meservey (Rostra CEO), Deepak Pathak (Skild AI CEO), Dylan Field (Figma CEO), and Lachy Groom (Physical Intelligence co-founder and chief operating officer) were angel investors. Turn Recorded Audio Into Useful Information With NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe Introduced today, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a new, open weight speech model that turns recorded conversations into useful information. Instead of needing multiple models for transcription, speaker labels and translation, developers can use one promptable model that handles all three, plus questions about the audio. It transcribes 40 languages, including seven Indic languages. Developers guide the model with plain-language prompts. For example, for a single recorded meeting, users can ask it to: “Transcribe this recording and label each speaker.” “Translate this audio into English.” “List what decisions were made in this meeting.” Prompts can also include product terms and formatting conventions, which helps the model handle specialized vocabulary in fields like healthcare, financial services and customer service. Because the weights are open, developers can choose where audio is processed, from a desktop to the cloud. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe ranks No. 1 on the Hugging Face Open ASR and No. 2 among open weight models on Artificial Analysis — delivering leading accuracy with approximately 4.3 billion active parameters, 80% fewer than the No. 1 open weight model, making high-quality, intelligent transcription more practical on local hardware.
